summary: THDC India Limited Pragati Puram, Bypass Road, Rishikesh-249 201 (Uttarakhand) **... Petitioner** Ms. Swapna Seshadri, THDCIL Mr. Utkarsh Singh, THDCIL Ms. Sneha, THDCIL Shri. Divyanshu Bhatt, Advocate, UPPCL Shri. Harsh V Shukla, Advocate, UPPCL 2. The Petitioner has set up a coal-based Thermal Power Project at Khurja in Bulandshahar District of the State of Uttar Pradesh, with a total capacity of 1320 MW, which comprise two units of 660 MW each. Furthermore, a 400-kV transmission line connecting the Project Switchyard to the PGCIL Aligarh Sub-station was implemented by the Petitioner for power evacuation from the Project, as per the 40 th meeting of the Standing Committee on Power System Planning held on 22.6.2018. The Petitioner is a subsidiary of NTPC Limited, with a shareholding pattern of 74.496% held by NTPC Limited and 25.504% held by the Government of Uttar Pradesh. The Petitioner has signed PPAs with the Respondent, UPPCL, on 31.12.2010 and with the Respondent, UPCL and the Rajasthan Discoms, on 4.1.2011. Further, the Ministry of Power (MOP), GOI vide its letter dated 15.11.2022, had allocated the power generated from the 3. The Petitioner vide affidavit dated 24.3.2025 has filed this petition in accordance with the provisions of Regulation 9(1) and Regulation 10 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, after serving a copy of the same on the Respondents. Accordingly, the annual fixed charges claimed by the Petitioner in respect of the generating station and dedicated transmission line are as under: 4. The Petitioner has also prayed for the grant of an interim tariff for billing purposes, subject to the determination of the final tariff. 5. During the hearing of the petition, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that Unit-I of the generating station achieved COD on 26.1.2025 and accordingly prayed for the grant of an interim tariff, pending the determination of the final tariff, in terms of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. None appeared for the Respondents. The Commission, after hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, directed the Respondents to file their replies, after serving a copy on the Petitioner. 6. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner sought the grant of an interim tariff of Unit-I of the generating station, from its COD, subject to adjustment based on the determination of the final tariff. The learned counsel for the Respondent, UPPCL, confirmed the filing of a reply in the matter. The Commission, after hearing the learned counsel for the parties, reserved its orders on the prayer of the Petitioner for the grant of an interim tariff in respect of Unit-I of the generating station, in terms of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 7. In order to enable the Petitioner to meet its ongoing financial obligations through a reasonable recovery of the cost of supply of electricity by the Petitioner to the Respondents and keeping in view that the interim tariff of the generating station will be subject to adjustment, based on the final tariff to be determined by the Commission, 8. Some of the provisions of Regulation 9(1) and Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff _Provided that for a new generating station or unit thereof or transmission system or element thereof, the applicant, through a specific prayer in its application filed under Regulation 9(1) of these Regulations, may plead for an interim tariff, and the Commission may consider granting interim tariff from the date of commercial operation after the first hearing of the application and where such interim tariff of the generating station or unit thereof and the transmission system or element thereof including communication system has been determined based on Management Certificate, the generating company or the transmission licensee shall submit the Auditor Certificate not later than 90 days from the date of Commercial Operation:_ _(3) If the information furnished in the petition is in accordance with these Regulations, the Commission may consider granting an interim tariff of up to ninety per cent (90%) of the tariff claimed in the case of a new generating station or unit thereof or transmission system, or element thereof during the first hearing of the application for billing purposes till the final tariff is determined by the Commission:_ 9. The normative O&M expenses claimed by the Petitioner towards the dedicated transmission line, Sub-station and Communication system are in line with Regulation 36(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. Accordingly, the same is considered for the purpose of the interim tariff as under: 25. The operational norms claimed by the Petitioner in terms of the provisions of the 2024 Tariff Regulations are as under: 30. The Petitioner has claimed Interest on Working Capital (IOWC) as per subclauses (a) and (d) of Regulation 34(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, as applicable for coal-based/ lignite-fired thermal generating stations and Transmission systems. The Petitioner has claimed the cost of coal for 50 days (20 days’ cost of coal towards stock and 30 days’ advance payment of cost of coal at the normative annual plant availability factor) in terms of the sub-clauses (i) and (iii) of Regulation 34(1)(a) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. The Petitioner has also considered the reference rate of 36. Accordingly, Petition No. 475/GT/2025 relating to the determination of tariff for Unit-I from its COD and the dedicated Transmission Line from the Project to Aligarh sub-station from its COD, i.e. from 26.1.2025 till 31.3.2029, shall be listed for hearing in due course, for which a separate notice will be issued to the parties. Meanwhile, the parties are directed to complete their pleadings in this matter.
title: Petition for determination of tariff of Khurja STPP (1320 MW) for the period from COD of Unit-I (26.1.2025) to 31.3.2029 and for the dedicated Transmission Line from Khurja STPP to Aligarh Sub-station from COD (26.1.2025) till 31.3.2029. THDC India Limited
